alerts.title: Abdominal pain may indicate TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list abdominal pain or discomfort as a presenting sign of TDF toxicity including lactic acidosis or severe hepatomegaly with steatosis, and recommend performing LFTs and RFTs when such symptoms occur. Patient is on TDF and reports abdominal pain today. Evidence for drug attribution: TDF can cause abdominal pain via lactic acidosis or hepatotoxicity. Evidence against: appetite is okay and no fever, which makes significant TDF toxicity less likely. Non-drug causes such as gastroenteritis or dietary causes should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Perform LFTs and RFTs as recommended by guidelines for TDF toxicity assessment. Evaluate for other causes of abdominal pain.

alerts.title: No monitoring labs ordered for abdominal pain
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for patients on TDF presenting with symptoms such as abdominal pain, LFTs and RFTs should be performed. The clinician's plan today does not include any laboratory orders despite the patient reporting abdominal pain. The most recent creatinine was 82 umol/L 78 days ago, but no LFTs are on record. The plan also lacks any symptomatic management or follow-up plan for the abdominal pain complaint.

evidence.recommended_action: Order LFTs and RFTs to evaluate abdominal pain in the context of TDF therapy, and document a follow-up plan.
